## p161 A2 — Request for Awaloff to come to Berlin

**Related source pages:** [p160 D1](160.md#source-p160-d1).

<a id="edition-cases-people-awaloff-return-request-request-for-awaloff-to-come-to-berlin"></a>



The first part addresses a political department with Oberkdo Mackensen; the matching source header carries the second part onto p161. The continuation requests that Fürsten Awaloff come to Berlin as soon as possible. LI, TSCHENKE, AWALOFF and STUMM remain source labels without added biographical identification.

Source: Childs, printed pp160–161 (PDF pages 163–164). [Source images and inputs](../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/inputs.json), [certificates](../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/certificates.json), [method and limitations](../experiments/nov8_radio_keys_and_reports/README.md). All indices below are zero-based.

<a id="source-p161-a2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-awaloff-return-request-p161-a2"></a>

### p161 A2

Header: `A) NKJ v LP (06.37 a.m., November 9th); FUER UKS (8/11) 2 TLE; 2 TL; RICHI-128`.

Native 128 includes printed C at 79 and 119, both filled explicitly. Its matching header and part 2 marking support continuation of p160 D1. LI, AWALOFF and STUMM remain labels.

The source has **128 slots** (126 valid coordinates). The native model has 128 slots / 64 plaintext positions: 62 fixed raw, 64 fixed after the stated edits.

**Cost:** 0 observed-coordinate substitutions; 2 printed-mask fills; 0 observed-coordinate exclusions; 0 mask exclusions; no inserted coordinates.

<a id="edition-cases-people-awaloff-return-request-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) reads the first part’s references as **Nr. 641** and **Telegramm Nr. 585**. The opposite assignment gives 541 and 686. These are conditional reference readings with no additional coordinate changes.

<a id="edition-cases-people-awaloff-return-request-shared-uncertainty-and-credit"></a>

### Shared uncertainty and credit

The two missing square cells `VF` and `XA` jointly contain `5` and `6`. Both complete assignments are retained as compatibility witnesses; every occurrence of a cell shares the same digit. The displayed `?` positions therefore must not be treated as independent digit choices. In p160 B2 one additional source coordinate remains unfilled; its domain can include letters as well as digits.

The published Nov7–9 period key and earlier OCR candidates are credited in the inputs. This edition adds source inspection, separate repair costs and exact readable-text mappings. It does not claim new recovery of the period key.

## p161 B1 — Urgent Constantinople embassy address; Gez. Stumm, part1 only

**Edition context:** Urgent embassy address: Constantinopel, signed Stumm.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-urgent-address-urgent-embassy-address-constantinopel-signed-stumm"></a>



Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged published Nov7–9 partial key retains its Lasry / Niebel / Kopal / Wacker attribution. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

<a id="source-p161-b1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-urgent-address-p161-b1"></a>

### p161 B1

This short message in Childs printed p161 (PDF page 164) contains an urgent embassy address and the signature STUMM. All **98 native source coordinates** are visible. Their **49 / 49 raw plaintext positions** are fixed without a historical coordinate edit, mask fill or geometry change.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-urgent-address-source-and-date-evidence"></a>

#### Source and date evidence

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — literal cleartext header:**

```text
9th NOVEMBER, 1918.
B) YZ, NKJ v LP (05.49 a.m., November 8th)
NKJ v LP AS BIS 0715
YZ v LP 0022 (9/11) 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-98
```

</details>

The receipt's **November 8th**, the subsection heading's **9th November**, and the internal **(9/11)** are retained separately. The edition does not force them into one date. The label says part 1 of two; an absent second part is not reconstructed.

The [native source detail](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/sources/p161_B_detail.png) shows the complete body and headers. Two mistakes in the current draft transcription were resolved by closer source inspection:

| Zero-based source index | Initial draft | Source reading | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 69 | W | V | The final V of `DVGXV` overlaps the preceding X; [high-resolution crop](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/sources/p161_B_lastV.png). |
| 96 | A | X | The final three-character group is `AXA`, with a crossed middle glyph between clear A forms; [high-resolution crop](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/sources/p161_B_final_group.png). |

These are corrections to the unpublished working transcription, not repairs to historical ciphertext. Keeping the mistaken final `AAA` would produce `DRINGENU`; the independently reviewed source `AXA` gives `DRINGEND` directly. The discarded draft and both intermediate readings remain in the certificate.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-urgent-address-native-reading"></a>

#### Native reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — native 98-coordinate frame, published Nov7–9 partial key:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTCONSTANTINOPELDRINGENDXGEZXSTUMM
```

</details>

The edited output is identical to the raw output. None of its coordinate pairs uses either unfilled key cell, VF or XA, so the unresolved global assignment of 5 and 6 has no effect on this body.

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Constantinopel. Dringend. Gez. Stumm.

`CONSTANTINOPEL` keeps its literal **C** spelling. `GEZ` stays abbreviated, and STUMM is not assigned an external identity.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-urgent-address-scope-and-verification"></a>

#### Scope and verification

The [p162 D1 address/signature fragment](162.md#edition-cases-people-constantinople-embassy-signature-p162-d1) provides related wording, but it has different source headers and the spelling `KONSTANTINOPEL`. Similarity does not establish that the two fragments belong to one telegram, and their missing parts are not joined.

The [inputs](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/inputs.json), [certificate](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/certificates.json) and [prior evidence](../experiments/nov9_urgent_embassy_address/prior_evidence.json) preserve every source row, the partial key's earlier provenance, the old disordered page OCR and the draft corrections. <a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-siegfried-and-osthoff-later-military-mission-recall-messages"></a>

<a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

An earlier Siegfried cancellation, [p135 A](135.md#edition-cases-people-siegfried-assignment-cancellation), directly supplies **45610** under the Nov4–6 key. If both orders cite the same reference, p161 C1’s observed XA/VF pairs fix **XA=5, VF=6**, so its reference reads **ZU2NR45610**. The two orders differ in wording and reception; [the complete comparison](../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) retains the alternative 46510. The erased date digit has the separately priced
completion below.

<a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-conditional-complete-siegfried-order"></a>

### Conditional complete Siegfried order

A separately priced date completion reads **MK 2.11**. The erased position has native domain **1GIKNY**, so 1 is its only numerical value if this is a day/month date. The distinct Osthoff recall on p161 D1 directly preserves `MKX2X11` in observed pairs. This supports the format and month, rather than treating the two orders as copies.

The completion supplies **F at printed dash 185**, changing `?G` to `FG`.
It adds one source-mask fill and no observed-coordinate substitution.
Together with the 45610 reference interpretation, C1 reaches **102/102
fixed labels** at **four observed substitutions and five printed-erasure
fills**. C2 is already an unchanged 77-label source reading.

**Readable German — complete conditional C1–C2 order; source abbreviations and spellings retained:**

> SS Doppel GR. HQ. MK. 2.11. Militaermiszion Konstantinopel. Zu 2 Nr. 45610. Komdo Oberlts Siegfried nach Tuerkei u deszen Zuteilung zur Milmiszion ist aufgehoben. AKO folgt. Allerh. Bef. Chef Milkab Frhr Marschall.

The two parts therefore have **179/179 conditional fixed labels**. The
spelling `DESZEN`, the abbreviation `u` and the received `MISZION` spellings
remain literal. The calendar reading does not force the reference
assignment: under the opposite 5/6 square the same date reads 2.11 while
the reference becomes 46510.

<a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-meaning-and-exact-scope"></a>

### Meaning and exact scope

C is an order cancelling Oberleutnant Siegfried's posting to Turkey and assignment to the Military Mission. D concerns Captain of the Reserve Osthoff: his Turkey posting and mission assignment are cancelled, and he is to be transferred to the replacement battalion of a railway regiment. The cabinet order will follow; the closing is from the Chief of the Military Cabinet, Frhr. Marschall.

These are readings of the telegrams. The edition does not establish a further biographical identity for either officer. The original abbreviations and the recurring spellings `MISZION` and `DESZEN` remain in the literal and edited strings.

Childs printed page 161 / PDF page 164 gives C at 05.57 a.m. on 9 November, `NR16 (9/11) 2 TLE`, and D at 06.05 a.m., `FUER YZ NR17 (9/11) 2 TEILE`. All four parts decrypt under the unchanged Nov7–9 key. Their printed lengths 204/154/254/190 exactly match the counted source slots.

<a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-cross-period-evidence-for-the-earlier-osthoff-edition"></a>

### Cross-period evidence for the earlier Osthoff edition

The earlier p149 A2 literal source had `UEM`, `ERSBKTL`, and `REGM1S`. Its already published editorial reading proposed `DEM`, `ERSBATL`, and `REGMTS`. The new p161 D2 source directly gives all three proposed letters under the other period key, without an edit to D2:

| Earlier p149 A2 position | Earlier raw → proposed | New p161 D2 observed pair | New original coordinate indices | Result |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|11|U→D|XV|58,135|Direct D in DEM|
|20|K→A|XD|49,107|Direct A in BATL|
|36|1→T|GV|80,118|Direct T in REGMTS|

Indices are zero-based. The certificate independently decrypts the selected older source, verifies that these were exactly its three preexisting editorial changes, and checks the new complete coordinate pairs. The older source's original repair costs remain unchanged.

The later wording is abbreviated and includes an additional raw `1` after `REGMTS`. It is not an identical ciphertext stream or a proof of a common original at every character. Its value is direct corroboration of the three specific earlier readings.

<a id="edition-cases-people-military-mission-recalls-remaining-uncertainty"></a>

### Remaining uncertainty

In the unchanged baseline edition, C1's date-like field remains `2X?1`: its erased position 19 has domain **1GIKNY**. The two question marks in `ZU2NR4??10` are different: they arise from the observed XA and VF cells of the published partial square, at plaintext positions 58 and 59. Their joint assignments are **56 or 65**, not independent choices that could both be 5 or both be 6. The conservative streams retain both assignments; the optional cross-period interpretation is given above.

The baseline C1 layer has four known-coordinate changes and four printed-erasure fills; the conditional date completion adds the fifth fill. The local `0→U` proposal before `DESZEN` alone costs two observed-coordinate substitutions; it is not a global reassignment of the digit0 key label. D1 has two word repairs, `KOMMRNDO→KOMMANDO` and `END→UND`. C2 and D2 are entirely unchanged source readings.

### Evidence and reproduction

[The input record](../experiments/military_mission_recalls/inputs.json) preserves all manual rows, literal irregular glyphs, source headers and crop-rendering metadata. [The certificate](../experiments/military_mission_recalls/certificates.json) retains all coordinate changes, masks, symbol domains, digit/J/Q/Y labels and round trips.
